richtext.rn58fd3410: Planet Indonesia (PI) is a non-profit organization founded in 2014, working with nearly 80,000 direct beneficiaries across rural, coastal, and marine ecosystems in West Kalimantan, Borneo, and supporting Indonesian communities to conserve forests and biodiversity. PI uses a holistic approach bridging the gap between social services, basic healthcare, financial access, and conservation needs to help communities access these services, creating more resilient livelihoods.

Rights

richtext.rn2ec6ddee:
Indonesia is highly vulnerable to climate change and is home to high levels of biodiversity loss and indigenous rights. The ability of rural communities to adapt to climate change depends on their access to basic services and the recognition of their land and resource rights.

The proposed programme will enable Planet Indonesia’s proven approach to scale up the long-term impact of existing partner villages and increase collaboration between local actors, communities, and government, including strengthening forest and marine conservation, and building better resilience in Tananua (in Flores Island) and by supporting five other local partners that have expertise in supporting indigenous rights and local communities.

PI will increase the climate resilience of 100,000 indigenous farmer and fisher families across national marine reserves and conservation areas. Activities include leveraging social enterprises to ensure stronger rights for communities; clarifying land tenure for communities and villages; integrated approaches to ensuring forest and marine ecosystem resilience; capacity building for local partners and organizations; training on sustainable harvesting techniques; connecting forest and marine ecosystem management to local markets and health services; and establishing a decentralized approach to capacity building and community engagement. This will help the project scale from supporting 10–20 villages per year to supporting the development of a minimum of 24 new community-led partner organizations. Key performance indicators: 100 village-level institutions.
